Hi Dana,

Thanks for the sync today — great to see the ProspectX team aligned on latency targets. As promised, attached is a compact runbook for our onboarding benchmarking session (sentry-runbook-v1.md). High level I suggest: 

- Smoke: single-user p95 and p99 checks (short)
- Throughput ramp: concurrency sweep to projected peak (2 hours total)
- Tail-latency stress: 1 hour with synthetic tail amplification

Targets (for this run):
- p50 generation latency <= 60ms
- p95 generation latency <= 220ms
- p99 generation latency <= 450ms
- Sustained throughput: 120 reqs/s at median 80 tokens per request

Can you confirm availability for Wed 2026-08-18 10:00 PT and the ENG contact we should include? I’ll loop in CS and Bench so we can capture telemetry and hand over results.

Attachments: sentry-runbook-v1.md (run steps), example payloads.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Team — heads up on Wed 10:00 PT benchmark with ProspectX (account PX-2026-489). Key asks from Dana: dedicated pool, p99 <= 500ms target, real payloads. Please see runbook attached; I’ll paste main checklist below.

Checklist (short):
- Monica: ensure telemetry ingestion is enabled (trace IDs, per-request timing, GPU utilization). We need token-level breakdown for their payload mix.
- Ben: reserve a dedicated capacity slot and confirm instance sizing (we should aim for same config ProspectX will use in prod).
- Laura: prepare the result template and latency plots; include token-distribution histograms.

Proposed acceptance gating: pass if p95 < 250ms and p99 < 500ms at sustained 120 reqs/s for 15 minutes. If p99 breaches but p95 holds, we capture artifacts and propose mitigations (kv cache tuning, quantization profile).

Also: bring the attachment 'latency-plots.pdf' placeholder in case they want a quick screenshot during the run.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana@prospectx.com>, ProspectX Eng <eng@prospectx.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Latency Sentry: run results and next steps (summary)

Dana / Priya — thanks again for running with us. Attached are the artifacts from the session: sentry-run-results.csv and latency-plots.pdf. Summary below (short):

Run details:
- Environment: ProspectX dedicated pool (c4-gpu-8x) provisioned via Redwood Dedicated
- Payload mix: median 82 tokens, 8% embedding+prompt combos (per sample file)
- Sustained window: 120 reqs/s for 20 minutes (we held steady for the window)

Key metrics (observed):
- p50: 58ms
- p95: 210ms
- p99: 480ms
- Max observed: 1.03s (2 requests during the tail-stress window)

Outcome: PASS per the acceptance gating (p95 < 250ms and p99 < 500ms). The two max spikes correlate with background KV-cache eviction events noted in GPU telemetry. Recommended mitigations included in the attached runbook: increase KV cache size by 20% and enable prefetch on the critical prefix set.

Next steps:
1) I’ll upload the full run logs to the shared drive link and attach a filtered CSV (sentry-run-results.csv).
2) Monica to prepare a short post-run write-up with the SLI labels and suggested config changes.
3) Dana / Priya: review mitigations and confirm if you want us to schedule a second pass after KV-cache tuning (we recommend a 2-hour follow-up verification).

If you want a quick 20-minute readout tomorrow, we can do that — otherwise we’ll wait for your confirmation on mitigations.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: sentry-run-results.csv (CSV stub), latency-plots.pdf (plots), sentry-runbook-v1.md
